borders.label: 边框 3 - Border 3
borders.description: The brand color is Fitbit Teal (`#00B0B9`) — it is the logo, the steps/activity color, the primary CTA, and the active tab. On dark backgrounds it brightens to a more luminous teal (`#21D9CE`) for text and links so it never muddies. The defining system characteristic is per-metric color coding: every health metric owns one fixed hue and keeps it everywhere it appears (tile icon, ring, chart line, detail screen). Steps/Activity = teal `#00B0B9`, Heart Rate = coral `#FF6B81`, Sleep = purple `#7C5CFF`, Daily Readiness = lime `#B8E986`, Active Zone Minutes = orange `#FF8A3D`, Calories = gold `#FFC233`. This means a user can recognize "that's my sleep data" purely by the purple, anywhere in the app — color is a navigational and mnemonic system, not decoration.

panels.title: 面向真实界面片段
panels.body: 按钮、输入、卡片和间距样例保持克制，便于比较不同主题的系统性差异。

do: 建议：Use the deep teal-black canvas {#001017}/{#002A3A} — cyan undertone, not neutral gray。
建议：Make Fitbit Teal {#00B0B9} the brand/steps/CTA; brighten to {#21D9CE} for text/links on dark。
建议：Give every metric its fixed hue and keep it everywhere (tile, ring, chart, detail) — color is a mnemonic。
建议：Make the big number the visual hero of every card (40–44pt bold, tight tracking)。
建议：Use progress rings as the recurring shape language for goals。
dont: 避免：use a neutral-gray dark theme — the canvas must carry the teal cast。
避免：let metrics share or swap colors — sleep is always purple, HR always coral。
避免：make labels/units compete with the hero number — keep them quieter and smaller。
避免：use clinical phrasing ("78% goal completion") — Fitbit speaks like a kind coach。
避免：use sharp or small radii — cards are 16–24pt, buttons are full pills。
